witness.note: Leges Henrici primi: Liebermann’s edited Latin text, from the manuscripts he names in Gesetze I, p. 547, note a, listed below
London, The National Archives (formerly the Public Record Office), E 164/2 (the Red Book of the Exchequer)
The original of the London collection, Leges Anglorum Londoniis collectae (c. 1210), which survives in copies
London, British Library, Cotton MS Claudius D.ii (Liebermann’s K, also K2)
John Selden’s manuscript, now lost (known from Twysden’s variants)
Roger Twysden, in Wheloc’s edition of Lambarde’s Archaionomia (Cambridge, 1644)
London, Guildhall (Corporation of London), a lost manuscript (there from at least 1639 to 1721), known only from the variants cited by earlier editors as “Lond”
Manchester, John Rylands Library, MS Latin 155

div.head: Hn 24.4
div.ab: Si prepositus regius in terra socnam habencium forisfactum prior sciat, non tamen habeat, nisi socnam illam excedat.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 562 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)

note.seg: Der Königsrichter darf innerhalb der Immunität in der Normandie einen Dieb wohl fangen, muss aber dessen Aburteilen ihrem Herrn überlassen (ausser wenn jener schon, bevor er sie betrat, gestohlen hatte); Très anc. cout. I 59—socam{2}—25 De privilegio.—Am Rande spät: Nota, curiam domino de tenente suo concedi in causa communi Rs

The royal judge may indeed seize a thief within an immunity in Normandy, but must leave his trial to its lord (unless the thief had already stolen before he entered it); Très anc. cout. I 59—socam{2}—25 De privilegio.—In the margin, in a late hand: Nota, curiam domino de tenente suo concedi in causa communi Rs

div.ab: If the king's reeve first knows of an offence in the land of those having soke, yet let him not have it, unless it exceeds that soke.
